question.text: SEBI orders an inspection of Anantha Capital AIF's records. What notice period must SEBI ordinarily give, and when can the notice be waived?

answer.text: 30-day notice mandatory in all cases; cannot be waived
No notice required — SEBI may inspect at any time
90 days' notice for Cat I and 60 days for Cat II
10-day notice in the normal course; MAY be waived by SEBI in the interest of investors by written order if SEBI is satisfied no notice should be given

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI shall give a 10-DAY notice to the AIF before ordering inspection under the AIF Regulations. However, in the interest of investors, if SEBI is satisfied that no such notice should be given, it may by an order in writing direct that inspection be taken up without notice. Sponsors, Managers and officers must co-operate, provide required information, and produce books/records. The Trap: Option A (30-day mandatory) is incorrect. Option B (no notice) ignores the default rule. Option C fabricates category-based tiers. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C covers the inspection regime. III-A/C Compliance tests similar SEBI inspection framework for brokers/intermediaries. Consequences of non-cooperation — SEBI directions can restrain fund-raising, direct refunds, or bar capital-market access. Manager's Pro-Tip: Pre-inspection readiness: (i) keep compliance files organised by theme (AI onboarding, UBO, CTR/STR, PPM amendments, quarterly reports), (ii) run mock inspection annually, (iii) maintain a single-point-of-contact compliance officer. If SEBI issues a no-notice order, cooperate fully — any defensive posture can escalate to prohibitory directions.
